findings.title: Etheric embodiment and hearing before the ear
findings.paraphrase: Steiner places dreamlike astral image consciousness before entry into etheric materiality. External etheric vibration then yields an organism-wide precursor of hearing before a separate organ exists.

findings.title: Reproduction, death and perceptual differentiation
findings.paraphrase: With condensation, reproduction changes from division to a locally mediated process, and the remaining body may disintegrate. Hearing localizes while touch still belongs to most of the body. Section 6 names the two early stages after the description of reproduction and death.

findings.title: External sunlight and the first eye rudiments
findings.paraphrase: Part of the light ether is withdrawn at solar separation and subsequently acts from outside. Steiner relates this altered dependence to the first organs receptive to sunlight, followed by further densification and the fire-mist human constitution. The chapter itself gives relative order, while Hyperborean placement is an editorial crosswalk.

findings.title: Reproductive force redirected to inward organs
findings.paraphrase: Steiner pictures older and newer reproductive forms coexisting. He connects density with redirecting part of the prior reproductive capacity into inward organs, mentioning the brain as an instrument of inwardly acquired cognition. He distinguishes early incomplete formation from readiness for spirit contact around mid-Lemuria.

findings.title: Mobility and senses before division into sexes
findings.paraphrase: In the late pre-division account, movement organs are comparatively developed. Hearing and touch are present earlier than light perception, which develops later in the life described. The text also situates extra-parental maturation and externally supplied heat before the later reproductive organization.

findings.title: Two forms of spiritual influence on early humanity
findings.paraphrase: Steiner assigns regulation of reproduction to advanced beings acting on the majority as instinct. A separate, less advanced group directs inner images toward the sensory environment, interrupting what he describes as an otherwise dreamlike spiritual life.

findings.title: Fire mist, upright form and divided guidance
findings.paraphrase: Thinking organs are prepared in the fire mist. After lunar separation and cooling, Steiner links upstanding posture and hand rudiments with altered functions of the upper body. He assigns lower-body guidance to Moon beings and renewed influence over developed personality to Luciferic beings.

findings.title: Moon separation, form and generation
findings.paraphrase: GA 13 describes the withdrawal of hardening forces as making individual embodiment possible. It relates emerging sexual differentiation to the distribution of seed and quickening capacities and describes lunar forces continuing from outside Earth.

findings.title: Breath, warmth and early bodily systems
findings.paraphrase: GA 13 attributes guidance of breath into the body to Sun beings. It distinguishes warmth currents as beginnings of blood circulation from an internal differentiation of air as a basis of the later nervous system. These are claimed antecedents, with no implication of modern anatomical completion.

findings.title: Interrupted embodiment, I and return
findings.paraphrase: Some souls can no longer inhabit hardening forms and continue elsewhere. Spirits of Form kindle the I, whose experience carries into body-free existence. As suitable forms become available after Moon separation, formerly displaced souls return over a long interval. The account distinguishes these first returns from repeat Earth incarnations.

findings.title: Lunar organization and two adverse influences
findings.paraphrase: The Moon beings shape the relation of I and bodies. Luciferic intervention grants greater control of consciousness images alongside error and dependence on astral impulses. Steiner separately introduces Ahrimanic influence through earthly forces and fear before its stronger mid-Atlantean manifestation.

findings.title: Different nighttime agencies act concurrently
findings.paraphrase: With alternating day and night, Steiner differentiates the nighttime sphere of activity around I and astral body from the simultaneous activity around physical and life bodies. Spirits of Form are common to both lists. This describes an early Earth rhythm, with a specific allocation of agencies rather than exclusive builders.

findings.title: Will, memory, speech and differentiated guidance
findings.paraphrase: GA 11 describes will-directed schooling and temple practice, and connects late Lemurian memory and elementary moral concepts to an account of women's role and of rhythmic utterance. The source uses gender essentialism and evolutionary ranking. Its local continuity claim reaches into early Atlantis while the fourth subgroup is in preparation.

findings.title: Volcanic destruction and a quieter precursor settlement
findings.paraphrase: GA 11 depicts volcanism destroying Lemurian territory while a relatively quiet area supports settlement and formation of an Atlantean precursor group. The account distinguishes the destructive environment from development in the refuge.

findings.title: Overlapping phases and memory-led naming
findings.paraphrase: Subgroups in Steiner's early taxonomy persist alongside successors. The first named subgroup emphasizes retained sense impressions, attachment to past experience and the development of naming already incipient in late Lemuria.

findings.title: Second phase and shared memory of deeds
findings.paraphrase: Steiner describes remembered personal achievement as a new basis of leadership and ancestor veneration. Recalled joint undertakings could bind groups in addition to ties of descent.

findings.title: Third phase, inherited authority and experimental settlement
findings.paraphrase: The third phase consolidates communal institutions, transmits leadership across generations, and uses remembered experience and experiments when establishing communities. Steiner sees an opening for personal appropriation of nature powers in the same process.

findings.title: Fourth and fifth phases change the role of power
findings.paraphrase: Steiner places intensified egoistic use of life forces in the fourth phase and the use of comparison and judgment to regulate desire in the fifth. He describes a tradeoff between inward combinatory thought and immediate command of living forces.

findings.title: Sixth and seventh phases differ in uses of thinking
findings.paraphrase: The sixth phase applies thinking more broadly to social order and law. The seventh is depicted as retaining greater attachment to inherited memory and belief in life powers while also developing thought. The source's extension of this typology to living populations is unsupported racial stereotyping.

findings.title: Pictorial memory, education and seed-force technology
findings.paraphrase: GA 11 presents imitation and remembered cases as a basis of judgment and education, with initiates treated separately. It claims growth forces in seeds could be redirected to devices under different environmental conditions. These are esoteric technological claims without archaeological or physical verification.

findings.title: Planetary affinities, sleep and distinct oracle practices
findings.paraphrase: GA 13 places the fuller differentiation of planetary affiliations in Atlantis. It distinguishes what sleepers and different kinds of initiates could experience through portions of the life-body, and calls the Christ oracle a prophetic stream within this wider field.

findings.title: Bodily stabilization and the mid-Atlantean crisis
findings.paraphrase: GA 13 connects bodily stabilization with variable plasticity, while naming misuse of growth and reproductive powers, including by some initiates, as a cause of destructive air and water changes. It separately emphasizes Ahrimanic distortion of sensory and postmortem experience from mid-Atlantis.

findings.title: Oracle preservation and the brain as instrument of thought
findings.paraphrase: The Sun oracle is credited with keeping and passing on etheric patterns of initiates. Among a successor group Steiner describes closer physical–etheric union, diminished older memory and the transformation of the brain into a needed instrument of thought and bodily self-awareness.

findings.title: Manu, independent understanding and a new type of initiate
findings.paraphrase: GA 11 describes selection of an eastward successor group, spiritual ideas addressed to its own thinking, and training of earthly thinkers as initiates. Later communities take on different forms as that teaching blends with older local inheritances.

findings.title: Two catastrophe narratives have distinct claimed mechanisms
findings.paraphrase: The Lemurian transition is connected to I-related use of fire under Luciferic influence. The Atlantean transition is linked to misuse of growth and generation under different conditions, with air and water effects and further migration. Both accounts are Steiner's esoteric prehistory.

findings.title: Atlantean inheritance, teachers and cultural overlap
findings.paraphrase: GA 13 describes the seven disciples of the Christ-initiate teaching people receptive to residual Atlantean perception. It explicitly distinguishes those people from later historical India and lets Indian cultural development continue concurrently with the next two dominant periods. Its claims about caste and spiritual descent belong to a historical esoteric account.

findings.title: Etheric emphasis in the individual-development stream
findings.paraphrase: GA 185 assigns etheric development to the earliest post-Atlantean individual in its second current, alongside an independent account of the age at which natural maturing ceases. This is a typological emphasis and has no bearing on established human biology.

findings.title: Persian orientation to work on Earth and the spirits of light
findings.paraphrase: Steiner portrays the sensory world as a field of action charged with spiritual significance. He distinguishes his primordial Zarathustra from later bearers of the name and associates the teaching about light with resisting Ahrimanic influence after death.

findings.title: The sentient body in the individual-development stream
findings.paraphrase: GA 185 assigns the sentient body to the second cultural period at the scale of typical individual development. The passage separately assigns the sentient soul to the following period at that same scale.

findings.title: Different initiatory responses to sensory immersion
findings.paraphrase: GA 13 describes related but distinct Egyptian and Chaldean-Babylonian cultural settings and ties increasing sensory interests to changing experience after death. Hermes is credited with preparing people during earthly life for the spiritual world, within Steiner's account of declining postmortem vision.

findings.title: Celestial observation and the Pergamum image
findings.paraphrase: GA 104 describes Chaldean observation of star motions as recognition of an intelligible pattern in visible nature. Pergamum represents this cultural period in the lecture's interpretive scheme.

findings.title: Sentient soul in one stream and a later analogy in another
findings.paraphrase: GA 185 assigns the sentient soul to the Egyptian-Chaldean period in its individual stream. In the separate whole-humanity stream, Steiner also calls fifth-age humanity analogous to the individual age band he associates with that same soul member.

findings.title: First Greco-Roman subperiod and inward independence
findings.paraphrase: GA 181 marks a first subperiod around 747 to 27 BCE. Steiner describes waning felt membership in a spiritual cosmos and connects more self-contained human experience with Greek culture. He presents the subsequent Christ event and secular culture as concurrent currents.

findings.title: Second Greco-Roman subperiod and dogmatic reception
findings.paraphrase: In a middle subperiod approximately 27 BCE to 693 CE, Steiner interprets the spread of external Christian doctrine as concurrent with difficulty understanding the Christ event through immediate cognition. This is the lecture's interpretation of church history.

findings.title: Third Greco-Roman subperiod and the split of faith and knowledge
findings.paraphrase: For the period approximately 693 to 1413 CE, GA 181 describes a separation between knowing by human concepts and accepting supersensible matters under revelatory authority. The boundary dates are approximate and the characterization concerns Steiner's European narrative.

findings.title: Golgotha as a second current within the cultural sequence
findings.paraphrase: GA 201 describes a continuous succession of cultures and a second current entering it at Golgotha, with its own proposed time symmetry. The historical sequence supplies the setting. Steiner assigns the Christ event a distinct spiritual origin.

findings.title: Golgotha, the I and the after-death world
findings.paraphrase: Steiner contrasts the cultivated visibility of spirit in Greek art with a shadowy postmortem experience. He places Moses among preparations for the highest form of the I, and credits the Christ event with limiting Ahriman's activity in the realm of the dead.

findings.title: Older and newer initiation overlap
findings.paraphrase: GA 13 describes residual natural supersensible faculties among some initiates during and beyond the fourth period. It also describes a newer way of developing cognition through human understanding and feeling, in which the Christ mysteries become central.

findings.title: Three concurrent scales of soul development
findings.paraphrase: GA 185 distinguishes humanity-wide maturation, the individual development of the consciousness soul, and a third current attributed to peoples. The first current is likened to the span in which an individual develops the sentient soul. The lecture's national character generalizations are historically situated and unsupported as descriptions of present peoples.

findings.title: Conscious social insight in the consciousness-soul age
findings.paraphrase: Steiner asks listeners to notice the human labor behind an everyday purchase and to revisit their own past from a more objective standpoint. He presents these exercises as ways to counter isolation and deliberately cultivate interest in other people.

findings.title: Long preparation, fifteenth-century start and later acceleration
findings.paraphrase: GA 13 describes preparation beginning in late antiquity, gradual emergence in the twelfth to fourteenth centuries, clearer emergence in the fifteenth, and rapid acceleration of intellectual development from the sixteenth. These thresholds describe different stages of one transition.

findings.title: Transformation of the third period's insights
findings.paraphrase: Steiner forecasts that what the third culture perceived dimly will recur in a form integrated with personal intelligence, feeling and the Christ mystery. The fifth and sixth periods are presented as especially consequential for this work.

findings.title: Etheric Christ and the exercise of free will
findings.paraphrase: GA 186 projects a reappearance of Christ in etheric experience and relates the response to voluntary spiritual action. It contrasts a misuse of the same powers that would bind activity to physicality. This is a teaching and prediction attributed to Steiner.

findings.title: The sixth culture begins as a possibility during the fifth
findings.paraphrase: GA 13 says the next period is slowly prepared during the current one. It projects a fuller accord between material civilization and spiritual life, anticipated wherever spiritual understanding is brought to sensory experience.

findings.title: A transformed Persian recurrence
findings.paraphrase: GA 106 describes a future cultural revival of the Zarathustra current in transformed circumstances. The recurrence is a correspondence between periods in Steiner's teaching, without a prediction that the specific institutions of historical Zoroastrianism return unchanged.

findings.title: Philadelphia and the transformation of wisdom into love
findings.paraphrase: In GA 104 the spiritual wisdom cultivated during the fifth cultural period is supposed to become an impulse of love in the sixth. Philadelphia signifies brotherly love, before the culmination of the seventh culture and the subsequent war.

findings.title: A transformed first-period pattern in the seventh culture
findings.paraphrase: Steiner describes an altered recurrence of ancient Indian culture. The social analogy in §14 contrasts inherited authority with future grouping under different conditions. It does not justify caste hierarchy or ranked treatment of contemporary people.

findings.title: Development continues as opportunities change
findings.paraphrase: GA 13 describes continued development in the seventh culture for souls prepared in the fifth and sixth, and more difficult conditions for others until a later time. A further upheaval comes after this cultural sequence.

findings.title: Earth epochs nested inside the physical form condition
findings.paraphrase: GA 104 places the seven great Earth epochs inside the fourth form stage of Earth's fourth condition of life, numbered 172 in this lecture. The seven post-Atlantean cultures belong to the fifth of those Earth epochs. The local 3–4–4 tally refers to completed subdivisions at three depths.

findings.title: Seals follow a transition beyond the seventh culture
findings.paraphrase: The lecture locates Philadelphia within the present set of cultural periods, the War of All Against All after that set, and the seven seals after the war. The seals and trumpets each have their own further division in this particular account.

findings.title: The first five seals and transformed cultural fruits
findings.paraphrase: GA 104a uses horse-and-rider pictures for the first four postwar periods, relating them to the first four cultures. The fifth period is pictured through the white robe and an astral body illuminated by the I. The source marks a gap at the end of the discussion of the fifth seal.

findings.title: Philadelphia and the sixth seal occupy different scales
findings.paraphrase: The lecture moves between a prewar cultural period associated with Philadelphia, its projected interventions in air and light, and an image of their fruits at the sixth seal. The claim that electrical waves and moral actions will cause earthquakes is unsupported.

findings.title: Trumpets and the ascent beyond physical form
findings.paraphrase: GA 104 places the seven trumpet subdivisions after the seals. It describes passage beyond the trumpets through astral and two Devachanic degrees, followed by densification into the next condition of life. This later Earth condition of life is at a different scale from Future Jupiter.

findings.title: Larynx, breath and the post-trumpet astral image
findings.paraphrase: Steiner takes the larynx and incoming breath as an example in his apocalyptic interpretation of bodily organs leaving astral forms. The claim belongs to his spiritual forecast and supplies no evidence for anatomical development or physiological function.

findings.title: Post-catastrophe choice, altered conditions and distant lunar work
findings.paraphrase: GA 13 projects seven periods after the convulsion and treats prior choices as preparation for altered spiritual conditions. It then describes lunar return and transformative assistance farther ahead, without supplying the seal-by-seal concordance or dating lunar return to a specific seal.

findings.title: Period arithmetic and the precision of calendar labels
findings.paraphrase: GA 184 calculates 2,160 years from its two stated epoch boundaries and obtains a midpoint by halving the interval. This supports the period length as Steiner's arithmetic convention. Dates obtained by projecting the interval onto other cultures are editorial derivatives, with a calendar-year-zero ambiguity around the BCE/CE crossover.

findings.title: The modern turning point in historical symptomatology
findings.paraphrase: GA 185 distinguishes the early-fifteenth-century change of soul life from familiar markers used in ordinary periodization. It connects late medieval social forms and universalist church life with the preceding period. This is a lecture interpretation of European social history.

findings.title: Early soul-member differentiation and the I
findings.paraphrase: GA 13 distinguishes an early Earth differentiation of sentient, intellectual and consciousness soul in the astral constitution from the culmination that allows the Spirits of Form to kindle the I. Its German §77 names Bewusstseinsseele where the Adams translation uses spiritual soul.

findings.title: The sevenfold pattern loosens and intersecting cycles remain in use
findings.paraphrase: In the 1924 priests' lecture Steiner says numerical regularity begins to shift with the consciousness-soul age. He still uses a seven-part archangelic cycle intersecting the longer cultural periods. The archive's §12 is printed in German in this English source view.

findings.title: Samael, Gabriel and Michael cross the cultural boundary
findings.paraphrase: Steiner names Oriphiel, Anael, Zachariel, Raphael, Samael, Gabriel and Michael in sequence from the time of Golgotha. Samael is already active at the beginning of the fifth culture. The lecture places Gabriel's cycle around 1471 and Michael's around 1879. It assigns longer cycles to beings of the middle hierarchy.

findings.title: Michael and the Christ event from two vantage points
findings.paraphrase: Steiner juxtaposes arrival of Christ on Earth with the farewell experienced by Michael's hosts on the Sun. Michael's later age signifies following Christ's descent, with a future role preceding Christ's deeds on Earth.

findings.title: War of All Against All as a moral transition
findings.paraphrase: The 1924 lecture places the war between great Earth epochs five and six, after cultures six and seven within the fifth. Steiner gives the moral catastrophe primacy and describes accompanying natural events as secondary. The comparison with ice-age events belongs to his teaching.

findings.title: Ephesus also symbolizes the Oriphiel interval
findings.paraphrase: Steiner can use the same church imagery for intersecting archangelic ages. Ephesus is associated here with the first smaller cycle, contemporary with the beginnings of Christianity. This supplies a second association alongside GA 104 III's first cultural period.

findings.title: The fifth-phase migration and bodily self-awareness
findings.paraphrase: This lecture begins an eastward migration in the fifth Atlantean phase, calls the formation of a successor group a last-third process, and connects physical–etheric change with capacity for first-person self-awareness. It also contains unsupported claims about ancestry and present-day populations.

findings.title: I-work on the astral body begins in dim consciousness
findings.paraphrase: GA 104 begins partially unconscious activity of the I on the astral body in Lemuria and early Atlantis, yielding what this translation calls the sensory soul. Later application of the I to other members is treated in the same lecture as a sequence.

findings.title: Etheric and physical work extend over later Atlantean phases
findings.paraphrase: The lecture places dim I-work on the etheric body during Atlantis, giving rise to the intellectual soul, and work on the physical body from the last third, giving rise to the consciousness soul. It associates the fuller individual impulse with Christ and distinguishes it from preliminary self-awareness.

findings.title: Completion of conscious astral transformation and the last trumpet
findings.paraphrase: Steiner distinguishes present beginnings of Manas from advanced spiritual self-development at the end of physical Earth. He connects survival into the astralized Earth with transformed etheric organization and interprets Pauline imagery in that context.

findings.title: Angels mediate individual and collective work
findings.paraphrase: GA 121 distinguishes individual work across incarnations from collective impulses. It describes Angels mediating between individual people and Archangels, with Spirits of Personality introducing a further influence at the scale of an age. The lecture's national character and ancestry claims are unsupported.

findings.title: Early Earth bodily currents and preparatory organ forms
findings.paraphrase: Steiner describes etheric humans condensing into mineral-bearing bodies and claims Earth's prior currents continue inward as blood vessels and nerves. He treats the modern umbilical cord as an analogue of a former bond with Earth and names preparatory forms of heart and brain. These are esoteric analogies and developmental claims.

findings.title: Atlantean heart rudiment in the lion group-soul account
findings.paraphrase: GA 104 connects a heart rudiment that later becomes the physical heart with the lion group-soul image. The lecture calls the condensed physical expression of an etheric pattern a horn. The source supplies an Atlantean bodily threshold in its own framework.

findings.title: Old Saturn heart germ in the Leo-region account
findings.paraphrase: GA 110 associates the initial heart germ with the arrest of motion in Old Saturn warmth and the Leo direction, naming activity of Thrones, Seraphim and Cherubim. The breastplate and Cancer discussion is adjacent and refers to a different structure.

findings.title: The I enters the intellectual soul around 333 in a 1924 account
findings.paraphrase: Steiner places an entry of the I into the intellectual soul around 333 CE, and reads the Arius–Athanasius controversy as an external expression. The lecture also phrases an interval as 333 years after Golgotha, leaving its calendar convention to be compared across editions. His reading is a spiritual interpretation of church history.

findings.title: Inherited conditions and the Christ impulse within individual life
findings.paraphrase: Steiner distinguishes inherited father-line impulses from a Christ or Son impulse that he says can be received through the soul within a person's earthly life. The latter belongs to the individual's development and operates at a different scale from a cultural period.

findings.title: Human spiritual fruits prepare Future Jupiter
findings.paraphrase: GA 104 compares Earth's previous preparation of bodily forms with the future formative influence of what people accomplish through soul and etheric transformation. This concerns preparation during spiritualized Earth for its future planetary condition.

findings.title: The fifth Atlantean phase and first I-soul impulse
findings.paraphrase: GA 104 distinguishes the first four phases in its group-soul account from the fifth, where it locates a first impulse toward individualized I-soul. It later reuses their animal-head imagery in its apocalyptic treatment, with an altered meaning.

findings.title: From the white robes to the seventh seal
findings.paraphrase: Steiner recaps the fifth and sixth postwar periods, then describes the seventh seal through divergent conditions: one group can act from an invisible sphere while another remains bound to matter. He introduces the Angels' earlier developmental path as an analogy for the first group's future capacities.

findings.title: Atlantis recapitulated as consciously regained clairvoyance
findings.paraphrase: In this lecture the seals era as a whole recapitulates Atlantis through consciously acquired clairvoyance. GA 104a II-9 additionally links individual seals with fruits of earlier post-Atlantean cultures. These correspondences have different chronological scales.

findings.title: Trumpet images and continuing physical conditions
findings.paraphrase: Steiner places the trumpets at a Devachanic level of hearing while describing a remaining Earth below. He explicitly numbers the first three images and the sixth. The darkening and first woe material sits between them in the prose and requires careful comparison before assigning every image a number.

findings.title: Individuality, spiritual fire and recurrence of Lemuria
findings.paraphrase: Steiner links receiving the Christ impulse with accepting distinct individualities and emerging from conditions of group soul. He compares the trumpet era with a spiritually transformed Lemuria, connecting its fire imagery with a higher rather than material condition.

findings.title: Two directions of reunion at the seventh trumpet
findings.paraphrase: The lecture projects a division in which the subtle portion of Earth reunites with the Sun while the dense portion combines with the Moon. Steiner calls it a transformed echo of the earlier solar separation. The resulting sequence requires comparison with GA 13's differently phrased reunion account.

findings.title: Christ as planetary spirit and Sorat as a named adversary
findings.paraphrase: Steiner links Zarathustra's earlier teaching, Golgotha and Christ's projected role in reunion with the Sun. He calls Sorat a solar adversary affecting the astral body and presents 666 as a name-number correspondence in his reading of Revelation.

findings.title: GA 346 uses two expressions for the 333 placement
findings.paraphrase: The published German text gives year 333 after Christ in §3 and 333 years after the Mystery of Golgotha in §14. It again identifies the year 333 in §§22 and 34. The two anchors occur in the German as well as the English and need to be recorded separately when reconstructing the lecture's schematic interval.

findings.title: The year 666 in the 1924 historical reading
findings.paraphrase: Steiner uses 666 as a historical year in his account of tensions in Christianity after 333. The lecture attributes spiritual opposition to Islam and an undifferentiated notion of Arab culture. These are sectarian esoteric claims and unsuitable as history or as descriptions of Muslims.

findings.title: Karmic continuity and sacramental transformation
findings.paraphrase: Steiner links the 333 placement to individual freedom and a loss of insight into connections between lives. He ascribes a common non-hereditary activity to the shaping of destiny across lives and to transubstantiation. His scenario in which Julian succeeds is explicitly a hypothesis.

findings.title: Sorat, the second 666 interval and the Templar episode
findings.paraphrase: The lecture gives 1332 as the second 666-year marker and interprets the earlier destruction of the Templars and death of Jacques de Molay in that thematic setting. The year 1332 is an arithmetic marker in Steiner's interpretation. The lecture supplies separate earlier dates for the institutional and biographical events.

findings.title: Michael's successive roles and the supersensible school
findings.paraphrase: Steiner places Michael with Aristotle and Alexander before Golgotha, then describes a supersensible school spanning the fourteenth through sixteenth centuries and preparing individuals for his modern Michael age. The dates concern his account of spiritual activity.

findings.title: The 1998 marker and distinct twentieth-century forecasts
findings.paraphrase: In 1924 Steiner projected an etheric manifestation of Christ in the first half of the twentieth century and activity of Sorat later in the century, naming 1998 as the third 666 marker. His wording also describes a rising threat before that marker. Treat these as recorded forecasts, with no judgment about people from physical features or politics.

findings.title: The Apocalypse as collective Christian initiation
findings.paraphrase: Steiner describes an initial period of transmission from witnesses, followed by a role for Revelation in Christian development. In his account the Apocalypse can work into the etheric body and initiate a collective process in which individuals may participate. He gives examples of this reception from the second through sixth centuries.

findings.title: Destruction of Jerusalem and the seed of a future formation
findings.paraphrase: The lecture places destruction of old Jerusalem after Golgotha and explicitly says the destruction could have taken place without that event. Steiner connects Golgotha with preparing a different future formation, the New Jerusalem, which he describes as developing from that point.

findings.title: Future city as a continuation of bodily formation
findings.paraphrase: Steiner presents the New Jerusalem as a future extension of the human being through spiritual knowledge and art. His explanation also assigns bodily nourishment to a speculative threefold system that conflicts with established physiology. The vision of a future city has no exact calendar placement here.
findings.chronological_placement: projected Earth development, exact subdivision unspecified

findings.title: Blood-marked garment and three modes of Christ activity
findings.paraphrase: Steiner reads Revelation 19 as portraying Christ inwardly, through the garment associated with Golgotha and the Logos, and through deeds in humanity. He explicitly describes the developing condition as lacking a specific year. Blood in this passage is scriptural symbolism.
findings.chronological_placement: projected Earth development, exact subdivision unspecified

findings.title: Three projected falls differ by their sphere of activity
findings.paraphrase: The sequence assigns the fall of Babylon to certain bodily conditions, the Beast and false prophet to direct Ahrimanic activity, and Satan to a claimed disruption of planetary order. The lecture gives a relative order for these outcomes. Its rhetoric about individuals and its astronomical claims are historically attributed esoteric material.
findings.chronological_placement: projected Earth development, exact subdivision unspecified

findings.title: Christ as balance in the reading of Revelation 19
findings.paraphrase: Steiner places Babylon on the Ahrimanic side, interprets the rejoicing above at its fall as Luciferic, and associates Christ with balance between the two. This passage links both influences with one apocalyptic scene.

findings.title: Three early Earth recapitulations and the novelty of Atlantis
findings.paraphrase: Steiner explicitly associates Earth's first three periods with higher-level repetitions of Old Saturn, Old Sun and Old Moon. He calls the fourth, Atlantean period new in that particular sequence. The source places this relation at the great Earth-epoch level.

findings.title: Greco-Roman culture repeats Atlantis at the soul level
findings.paraphrase: The lecture compares Atlantean accounts of perceiving spirit in solid-liquid conditions with Greco-Roman perception in liquid-airy conditions. It relates the 333 and 666 markers to earlier, unspecified Atlantean upheavals by analogy. This is a different recapitulation from the postwar seals account.

findings.title: Anticipated conscious images in the Michael age
findings.paraphrase: Steiner invokes inner warmth and the etheric Christ to project conscious visionary images of earlier Earth conditions. He distinguishes these images from an Atlantean physical experience and a Greco-Roman soul experience. The account is a forecast made in 1924.

findings.title: Mid-Atlantean solar birth and stages of I-awareness
findings.paraphrase: Steiner associates the solar birth image with a gradual awakening of I-awareness in Atlantis. He distinguishes continued activation from outside through the Sun from later inward residence of the I in the fourth post-Atlantean age. This supplies a development spanning two great Earth epochs.

findings.title: Michael and dragon imagery across Atlantis and later periods
findings.paraphrase: Steiner connects a struggle of Michael in the Sun with mid-Atlantean changes, then compares the image with later mythological forms and a projected renewed vision in the Michael age. His account also connects the seven-headed beast with the Atlantean transition. These references are multiple uses of images across times.

findings.title: German comparison of the formation of the soul members
findings.paraphrase: The German gives Empfindungsseele for the result of early I-work on the astral body, Verstandes- oder Gemütsseele for work on the etheric body in Atlantis, and Bewußtseinsseele for work on the physical body from late Atlantis. This sequence and agency coexist in the source record with the differently structured GA 13 IV §77 account.

findings.title: German distinguishes I-soul impetus and heart predisposition
findings.paraphrase: The German has a first impulse toward Ich-Seele in the fifth Atlantean period and uses Anlage for the heart predisposition in its lion group-soul account. It describes the physical heart as a later outcome. The German supports the separation between the predisposition and the later physical organ.

findings.title: The seven Earth life conditions and their distinct kingdoms
findings.paraphrase: The lecture names three elemental conditions followed by mineral, plant, animal, and human life conditions. It distinguishes humanity's esoteric mineral condition from ordinary biological classification, and warns against applying these Earth names to the analogous Saturn and Sun conditions.

findings.title: Physical form is the middle of seven forms within a life condition
findings.paraphrase: The form sequence descends through higher Devachan, lower Devachan and astral to physical. It then ascends through transformed astral, lower and higher Devachan. The mineral life condition extends through those forms. The German clarifies that three completed states in §25 are life conditions, each with seven forms.

findings.title: Representative life on Old Saturn
findings.paraphrase: Steiner answers how Old Saturn could include life conditions before the human etheric body. He attributes the representative life to the activity of higher beings who permeate the human rudiment with their own members, while the human germ lacks independent life.

findings.title: Planetary intervals and successive forms
findings.paraphrase: Steiner describes spiritual intervals between planetary embodiments. The globes in this diagram are successive forms of an evolving sphere. He describes astral Earth in connection with the bowls of wrath and qualifies the diagram as conceptual scaffolding.
findings.chronological_placement: projected Earth development, exact subdivision unspecified

findings.title: Five levels in the numerical schematic
findings.paraphrase: GA 104 adds two depths beneath the form level: great epoch and smaller period. It explicitly illustrates this with physical Earth, the seals and trumpets, and the seven post-Atlantean cultural periods. The numerical total 16,807 describes the idealized full five-depth scheme, with far fewer intervals individually described in this lecture.

findings.title: Four early heads, three later heads and ten horns
findings.paraphrase: Steiner connects the first four Atlantean phases to group-soul images and the crossing into the fifth to emerging individuality. His account locates conscious perception of sexual difference at an Atlantean threshold and uses the head-and-horn imagery again for projected astral Earth.

findings.title: The fifth-seal omission is also marked in German
findings.paraphrase: At the same point after the white garment image, the German source has a visible omission marker. Both checked English versions preserve a gap. This supplies no evidence about the wording that would have occupied it.

findings.title: Post-trumpet branches and Mammon in the lower astral world
findings.paraphrase: Steiner distinguishes higher astral and eventual Devachanic development from a lower astral branch. He names Mammon as a spirit of obstacles and places reunion with the Sun after the trumpet period for those capable of it.

findings.title: Luciferic benefits, costs and later redemption
findings.paraphrase: Steiner associates the Lemurian intervention with deeper material involvement and the possibility of human independence. The beings act through the astral body and experience aspects of development there that they missed earlier. He projects later human participation in their redemption.

findings.title: Opposing figures and a renewed act of assistance
findings.paraphrase: Steiner distinguishes left-behind Luciferic spirits, humans whom he treats as having remained behind without conscious choice, and those he depicts as deliberately turning spiritual powers toward selfish aims. He projects a return of spiritually developed humans from union with the Sun to assist the second group.

findings.title: Jupiter-Earth, Venus-Earth and Vulcan-Earth are anticipations within Earth
findings.paraphrase: In this lecture Steiner says Earth's rounds look back to Saturn, Sun and Moon and anticipate later planetary conditions. He places renewed opportunities for assistance on Jupiter-Earth, a last opportunity on Venus-Earth, and its closing by Vulcan-Earth. The German explicitly says the anticipations occur within the actual Earth condition.

findings.title: Art, Babylon and the future New Jerusalem
findings.paraphrase: The text places the casting away of evil in a Venus-Earth setting and calls this the Fall of Babylon. It also treats present human artistic work as formative for a future New Jerusalem and mentions a Jupiter existence. The boundaries of that final reference remain open.

findings.title: Etheric head enters and gradually supports I-development
findings.paraphrase: The lecture ties late Atlantean preparation to a changing relation of etheric and physical head and distinguishes that development from Golgotha's more significant impulse. German Hereinrücken indicates an inward movement where SOL English says emergence. The source's analogy involving hydrocephalus has no standing as modern medicine.

findings.title: Preparatory transformation and the higher members
findings.paraphrase: Steiner describes transformation of astral, etheric and physical bodies into Spirit Self, Life Spirit and Spirit Man. He distinguishes preparatory work through higher beings and initially unconscious work from subsequent conscious activity. The same passage links earlier transformations with the three soul members.

findings.title: Six cultural emphases and preparation for Philadelphia
findings.paraphrase: The sequence gives etheric body, astral body, sentient soul, intellectual soul, consciousness soul and Spirit Self as successive organizations permeated by the I. The Philadelphia passage associates Spirit Self and etheric Christ recognition. It does not name a seventh member in this sequence.

findings.title: How Philadelphia prepares the sixth-seal community
findings.paraphrase: Steiner connects the fourth to sixth seal periods with development of the three soul forces and preparation for Manas. He derives the 144,000 symbol through numerical interpretation and links a community prepared during Philadelphia with the sixth seal.

findings.title: Babylon, the Venus-Earth count and the eighth sphere
findings.paraphrase: Steiner juxtaposes the sixth seal and a sixth condition at a different scale. He attributes a separation to an eighth sphere to the Venus-Earth setting and invokes the two witnesses in a future act of assistance. The work uses a different predicate for Babylon here than the previous lecture, and gives no modern absolute date.

findings.title: Future heart and speech-organ transformations
findings.paraphrase: Steiner connects future human development with a changed heart function and a projected reproductive capacity of speech. He notes an anatomical feature of heart muscle before making a separate esoteric forecast. The forecast carries no empirical or medical authority.
findings.chronological_placement: projected Earth development, exact subdivision unspecified

findings.title: Universal cooperation and the occult image of homelessness
findings.paraphrase: Steiner uses homelessness as a technical term for gaining perspective on attachments to locality or heritage. He envisages a later common human task in which contributions can be made freely. This terminology refers to his initiatory concept.

findings.title: Preparatory soul activity and later threefold transformation
findings.paraphrase: GA 121 describes present beginnings of Spirit Self, distinguishes the three preparatory soul members, and links the future work of the I on the astral, etheric and physical bodies to Spirit Self, Life Spirit and Spirit Man respectively.

findings.title: Archangelic activity and succession of Spirits of the Age
findings.paraphrase: Steiner distinguishes Angels' human stage on Old Moon from present physical humanity. He attributes transformation toward Life Spirit to Archangels and associates Spirits of Personality with changing eras. In his account they hand over offices and return after other spirits have held them.

findings.title: Population movements in an etheric account of regions
findings.paraphrase: Steiner treats regional etheric auras as changing with migration, giving the European Migration Period as an example. He distinguishes the activity he attributes to Archangels from physical terrain and assigns a different temporal pattern to an individual etheric aura. The account's national temperament typology is historically situated and unsupported.

findings.title: The speech apparatus and two groups at an archangelic level
findings.paraphrase: Steiner attributes national temperament to normally developed Archangels and the shaping of the larynx and speech apparatus to cooperation involving Spirits of Form who retained an archangelic mode of activity. He associates another action of Spirits of Form with shaping the brain for saying I. These are attributed esoteric claims about human organs.

findings.title: Outer historical conditions and inward shaping of thought
findings.paraphrase: GA 121 distinguishes normally developed Spirits of Personality associated with historical circumstances from Spirits of Form retained at another developmental level and associated with shaping thought from within. The lecture presents both influences as potentially concurrent.

findings.title: Three modifications of the astral body and degrees of I-awareness
findings.paraphrase: The lecture treats the three soul members as modifications within the human astral body and relates them to dim, emerging, and clear I-awareness. It associates analogous modifications of Archangels with their etheric bodies. This is a description of organization and experience.

findings.title: Mediation, differential roles, and retained modes of activity
findings.paraphrase: Steiner gives Angels a mediating role and distinguishes coordination across several hierarchies from their members' own developmental work. The discussion also assigns racial categories to spiritual influences in a historically situated typology. Its claims about ancestry or national character are unsupported.

findings.title: Astral germ and the first etheric organization
findings.paraphrase: GA 11 depicts an astral germ carrying forces from earlier conditions. Astral humans chiefly work from outside on their etheric counterparts, forming organs and awakening etheric life. The chapter names this opening condition Polarean.

findings.title: Air-like matter, chemical ether, water and light ether
findings.paraphrase: In GA 11 an air-like condensation leaves the chemical ether alongside the earlier life ether. The air-like condition subsequently differentiates into air-like and watery conditions, and light ether differentiates from chemical ether. Descendants of earlier forms continue alongside newer human-like, animal-like and plant-like organizations.

findings.title: Watery conditions already appear before solar separation in GA 11
findings.paraphrase: The essay names water, air and three ethers before narrating the Sun's separation. Greater densification and an internal source of heat follow. GA 13 IV §66 places solar separation before watery incorporation in the narrated sequence, so the two accounts retain separate stage orderings.

findings.title: Fire-mist enables concurrent embodiment and distinct activity
findings.paraphrase: GA 11 gives human beings a dim conscious life and externally directed activity within the fire mist. It gives higher beings a shared medium in which their decisions can organize denser conditions. The source describes upward development of human understanding and downward extension of higher beings' activity at the same time.

findings.title: Reproduction and understanding follow two different agencies
findings.paraphrase: The chapter transfers lunar influence to external regulation of reproduction after the Moon's separation, while describing renewed Luciferic activity in awakening human understanding. It identifies the preceding fire-mist period as an interruption in that Luciferic activity and leaves more precise identifications for later chapters.

findings.title: Inherited organization and solar separation in GA 13
findings.paraphrase: GA 13 distinguishes recapitulation of the three earlier bodies, a spiritual interval, and a new astral descent with physical laws already present. In its material sequence the Sun separates from the fire-air Earth before Earth incorporates water. Sun beings then influence Earth from outside and the text relates this to alternating consciousness.

findings.title: The trumpets on a consciousness-soul timescale
findings.paraphrase: In 1924 Steiner explicitly distinguishes the trumpets as an interpretation of consciousness-soul development from the longer development of the astral body and humanity that he had emphasized in 1908. He calls the processes interwoven and places his present within the trumpets only on the narrower scale.

findings.title: The sixth trumpet and an edition-dependent decade
findings.paraphrase: German §6 refers to the beginning of the forties immediately after §5 discusses 1843–44. The SOL English inserts 1940s. Section 23 describes the sixth trumpet as already underway for the 1924 audience. The narrower chronology concerns Steiner's interpretation of consciousness-soul development.

findings.title: Golgotha to the Crusades as a smaller seals epoch
findings.paraphrase: In Steiner's smaller historical interpretation, the period from Golgotha to the Crusades belongs to the opening of the seals and the Crusades mark a transition to the trumpets. He interprets changing Christian institutions and mystical inwardness through these images. The lecture's sectarian judgments belong to its esoteric interpretation.

findings.title: The 1413 boundary and the antecedents of the trumpet motifs
findings.paraphrase: The lecture dates the beginning of the consciousness-soul age to 1413 on Earth while tracing the associated trumpet motifs back to the Crusades. It places a projected seventh trumpet near the end of the twentieth century on this same narrower scale. Its language about the absence of an I cannot be used to classify people.

findings.title: An individual threshold and a historical threshold for humanity
findings.paraphrase: Steiner presents the individual crossing of the threshold as a differentiation of spirit, soul, and body, and claims humanity as a whole undergoes a related process in the consciousness-soul age. He reads the cloud-borne face, rainbow, and fiery feet of Revelation 10 as images of thought, feeling, and bodily life.

findings.title: The 2,160-year period and Steiner’s proposed textual change
findings.paraphrase: Steiner gives an approximate cultural span as one twelfth of 25,920 years and proposes reading 2,160 days in two passages of Revelation transmitted as 1,260. The German confirms the proposal. The source supplies Steiner's conjectural reading, with no independently verified textual emendation established here.

findings.title: The sea of glass as a projected Earth change
findings.paraphrase: Steiner interprets the sea of glass as a future reflective watery condition associated with a reduction of the present seasonal extremes. He attributes a role to collective human inner activity. This is a prediction in the lecture's esoteric cosmology.
findings.chronological_placement: projected Earth development, exact subdivision unspecified

findings.title: Divine love, light, and the future bowls
findings.paraphrase: The lecture associates divine equilibrium with love manifesting outwardly as light. It interprets the bowls in a future age as an altered expression of that love after it meets materialistic human conditions. The lecture describes destructive results as removing obstacles to further development.
findings.chronological_placement: projected Earth development, exact subdivision unspecified

findings.title: Atlantean catastrophe and a future moral–natural correspondence
findings.paraphrase: Steiner uses the Atlantean catastrophe as an earlier instance of what he regards as human conduct altering natural phenomena. He forecasts a related process in the future and connects it with the bowls. Both the retrospective cause and the physical forecast are claims of his esoteric interpretation.
findings.chronological_placement: projected Earth development, exact subdivision unspecified

findings.title: Comet imagery in the 1924 Apocalypse interpretation
findings.paraphrase: Steiner connects the beast motifs with comet forms and describes Biela's comet and the 1872 meteor shower in relation to supposed activity in the astral body. He also associates the imagery with Michael's approach in the late 1870s. The astronomical and therapeutic statements are attributed esoteric claims.

findings.title: The beast in 1933 and understanding the etheric Christ
findings.paraphrase: The 1924 lecture gives a qualified 1933 catastrophe scenario in its comet interpretation and associates 1933 with the beast motif before fuller understanding of the etheric Christ. The scope differs from the 1998 Sorat marker in lecture VIII. The passage records a forecast and spiritual interpretation.

findings.title: Initiation sequence through seals, trumpets, and hierarchies
findings.paraphrase: Steiner treats seals and trumpets as stages of perception in an initiatory reading, with elemental effects giving way to an encounter with the second hierarchy and its harmony. He associates the next spiritual region with angels, archangels and Archai. This is a sequence of perception in addition to historical or planetary readings.

findings.title: Breakdown, glandular imagery and bowls as macrocosmic analogy
findings.paraphrase: The lecture associates bodily breakdown with spiritual activity and compares excretion to the vessels of wrath. It explicitly uses the word gland in a microcosm–macrocosm correspondence. Its claims about brain processes and the body are esoteric, and the image does not establish a physiological mechanism.

findings.title: Three scales of activity in the third hierarchy
findings.paraphrase: Steiner assigns care of an individual's soul to angels, guidance of groups to archangels, and movement of events from age to age to Archai. He depicts these beings together as the expression of higher hierarchies.

findings.title: Intellectuality in the consciousness-soul age and later development
findings.paraphrase: Steiner describes intellectuality entering individual human activity in the current age, then reaching deeper emotional and passionate life. He associates a later Jupiter stage with its extension into human physicality. The lecture leaves the future placement at the named stage level.

findings.title: Independent intellect as a point of vulnerability in GA 346
findings.paraphrase: Steiner identifies an Ahrimanic power called Satan in this passage, assigns it rank among the Archai, and links its activity to the independence of human intellect. He distinguishes present human susceptibility from exceptional or future possibilities involving angelic beings. The proposed human response depends on voluntary spiritual alignment.

findings.title: Gog and Magog as a conditional group-level sequence
findings.paraphrase: Steiner interprets Gog and Magog as groups exposed to a projected temptation operating through intellect. He gives Michael and freely directed human spiritual activity a role in the outcome. The lecture presents an alternative adverse future contingent on human action without assigning a calendar date.
findings.chronological_placement: projected Earth development, exact subdivision unspecified

findings.title: Sacramental reading of the three hierarchies
findings.paraphrase: The closing lecture interprets transubstantiation as an encounter with the hidden work of the first hierarchy in physical substance, with Christ leading toward a second-hierarchy disclosure and a region associated with the third hierarchy and the Holy Spirit. This is a sacramental account of spiritual perception.

findings.title: Old Saturn and variable trance-like awareness
findings.paraphrase: Steiner assigns the rudimentary human organization a predominant awareness duller than dreamless sleep. He explicitly allows variation within Saturn and says other beings then possessed what he calls human consciousness.

findings.title: Old Sun and the dreamless-sleep analogue
findings.paraphrase: Steiner compares the predominant Old Sun awareness to present dreamless sleep and to the condition he attributes to plants. These are analogies within his account of consciousness.

findings.title: Old Moon image awareness and its Atlantean reprise
findings.paraphrase: Steiner describes vivid images corresponding to the spiritual environment, distinguishes them from fragmented present dreams, and says this condition was repeated during Atlantean evolution as Earth developed waking object consciousness.

findings.title: Jupiter preserves waking awareness in conscious imaging
findings.paraphrase: In Steiner’s projection, Jupiter consciousness combines image perception with the clear awareness proper to Earth. He describes initiation as anticipating this combination.

findings.title: Venus and inspired tonal consciousness
findings.paraphrase: Steiner projects an inspired awareness in which an inner character appears as a unified tone and beings formerly experienced as images are perceived as tonal structures.

findings.title: Vulcan and intuitive consciousness with individuality
findings.paraphrase: Steiner calls the projected Vulcan state intuition in a technical sense. The soul participates inwardly in beings within its field of perception and retains its individuality.

findings.title: Plant forces, laboratory creation and future ethics
findings.paraphrase: Steiner projects that understanding plant growth forces will allow the creation of plant forms without seeds. He frames legitimate use as requiring a transformed moral life and links the projected kingdom to shared well-being. These are esoteric forecasts.
findings.chronological_placement: projected Earth development, exact subdivision unspecified

findings.title: The three completed counts in Steiner’s 344
findings.paraphrase: Steiner counts three completed forms of the fourth life condition, four completed great epochs of the physical form and four completed post-Atlantean cultural periods. He reads the three digits individually.

findings.title: 66, 466 and 666 in the longer trumpet account
findings.paraphrase: Steiner puts 66 after six trumpets and treats the seventh-trumpet disposition, associated with 466, as still reversible for a time. He reserves final separation for a later 666. The lecture’s adjacent descriptions use different scale terminology for that last formula.

findings.title: Conditional prophecy and free choice
findings.paraphrase: In the authored essay, Steiner distinguishes the purported lawfulness of a result from the free choices that may establish its conditions. He presents spiritual foresight as compatible with freely brought-about events and claims it can guide ideals.

findings.title: Seven embodiments and living intervals of rest
findings.paraphrase: Steiner presents humanity and its sphere as co-developing through three past, Earth and three future embodiments. In the intervening pralayas life persists, though conditions elude the senses developed in the open cycles.

findings.title: Saturn awareness is dim in clarity and broad in reach
findings.paraphrase: Steiner distinguishes the breadth of awareness from its clarity. He describes Saturn as broader and dimmer than Earth, and distinguishes a trance comparison from a clairvoyant’s claimed retention of waking clarity.

findings.title: Recapitulated awareness changes form on Sun and Moon
findings.paraphrase: Steiner has Sun develop the Saturn predisposition again in changed form before its own awareness. Moon subsequently repeats the Saturn and Sun stages in smaller cycles before attaining an image awareness keyed to its surroundings.

findings.title: Older mystery rites and withdrawal of direct divine presence
findings.paraphrase: Steiner describes a claimed ancient mode of direct contact between gods and officiants, tied to celestial timing. In his semi-ancient mode the gods send powers and the officiants use preserved substances as a means of ritual knowledge. The passage gives a relative order.

findings.title: Four levels of ritual reception and the conscious I
findings.paraphrase: Steiner connects the first three mystery modes to physical, etheric and astral experience. He situates the first Communion within the third mode and describes the modern task as consciously uniting the I with Christ and grasping the rite and revelation.

findings.title: Saturn warmth boundary and the experience of wonder
findings.paraphrase: Steiner depicts early warmth differentiation as a warmer interior and a cooler warmth envelope. He calls its inward experience wonder and uses Alpha and Beta to represent warmth-human and first enclosure.

findings.title: Vulcan completion and Christ at Earth’s midpoint
findings.paraphrase: Steiner interprets Alpha and Omega as the initial human being united with its whole world at Vulcan. He describes Christ at Golgotha as already at the stage humanity would reach at that endpoint.

findings.title: Twenty-four Elders and the four living figures
findings.paraphrase: Steiner interprets the Elders as enduring revelations of successive representatives, including some still to come, assembled around Christ. The four living figures signify humanity as a whole in this scene. The passage supplies no dated sequence of twenty-four eras.

findings.title: Loss of remembered pre-existence and persistence of fourth-period habits
findings.paraphrase: Steiner attributes awareness of pre-earthly life to the first three cultural periods and a growing sense of earthly boundedness to the fourth. He says fourth-period habits persist into the fifth through education and public life.

findings.title: Consciousness soul and an awareness of continuous dying
findings.paraphrase: Steiner predicts that people will increasingly experience dying as active throughout life. His fire image concerns the felt transition into wakefulness and the inward cost of awareness. The reference belongs to his phenomenology of consciousness.

findings.title: Sixth cultural period and changed perception of nature
findings.paraphrase: Steiner distinguishes the fifth period’s change in self-perception from a sixth-period change in how the surroundings are experienced. He interprets falling stars in terms of awareness of spiritual activity behind the visible heavens.

findings.title: Sardis as the fifth church and fifth seal in the smaller reading
findings.paraphrase: Steiner applies the Sardis image and the fifth seal to the modern fifth cultural period and urges his priestly audience to realize the task in daily life. GA 346 XIII separately explains the smaller scale used in this course.

findings.title: The free I as a capacity for love and hardening
findings.paraphrase: The lecture traces the I to differentiation from group-soul consciousness. Steiner interprets the two-edged sword as the capacity to deepen free individuality or harden it into selfish conflict. He assigns the War of All Against All to the second trajectory.

findings.title: The sixth cultural period prepares a later community
findings.paraphrase: Steiner associates Philadelphia with spiritual brotherhood and treats souls formed in the sixth cultural period as a foundation of post-war cultures. He describes the transition through an analogy with his account of the end of Atlantis.

findings.title: A reversible separation and the future educational task
findings.paraphrase: Steiner assigns a future effort to draw back separated people to those he calls disciples of Manichaeism. He still allows recovery at the astral transition. The passage records his reconstruction of Manichaeism and its projected role.

findings.title: Late Lemurian to Atlantean migration in the 1908 account
findings.paraphrase: Steiner distinguishes early ethereal Earth conditions from the later epochs and attributes the founding of Atlantean populations to an emigrating minority of the last Lemurian group. This is an esoteric prehistory with racialized terminology.

findings.title: Christ-derived love and the astralization of Earth
findings.paraphrase: Steiner associates the physical-to-astral transition with the capacity to dissolve material form through love. He interprets seven bowls of wrath through the expulsion of hardened matter. The account places this transition before its final irreversible outcome.
findings.chronological_placement: projected Earth development, exact subdivision unspecified

findings.title: Transformation of the three bodies through the I
findings.paraphrase: Steiner calls the I’s transformation of the astral body Spirit Self, of the etheric body Life Spirit and of the physical body Spirit Man. Earth permits development of these members, while their full development belongs to a more distant future.

findings.title: The separated Earth and the horns as hardened limbs
findings.paraphrase: After the trumpets Steiner describes an astral Earth and a separate portion unable to participate in its transformation. His reading of the beast’s horns treats them as hardened physical limbs of that portion’s inhabitants.
findings.chronological_placement: projected Earth development, exact subdivision unspecified

findings.title: Spirits of Form, retarded Spirits of Movement and early awareness
findings.paraphrase: Steiner credits the Spirits of Form with bestowing the capacity for I-consciousness. He assigns earlier perception of the physical environment in individual development to Spirits of Movement that act at the rank of Form. Ages and stages belong to the lecture’s esoteric account.

findings.title: Lemurian bodily differentiation and a cultural-repetition thesis
findings.paraphrase: Steiner associates Lemurian bodily differentiation with locality and reproduction under beings he calls abnormal Spirits of Form. He then describes post-Atlantean cultural stages as changed repetitions of previous bodily conditions. The racial and geographic claims are historically situated and unsupported.

findings.title: Early physical growth as a recurrence of Saturn
findings.paraphrase: Steiner connects the physical organization from birth to the change of teeth with an individual reprise of Old Saturn. He distinguishes that model of repeated physical development from the distinctive Earth work of the Spirits of Form on the I.

findings.title: Interval of independent development and four mystery stages
findings.paraphrase: Steiner says direct mystery work once withdrew to leave humanity largely to its own resources. He claims that interval’s forces have become exhausted and presents modern ritual as a new stage. He deliberately introduces his four successive mystery modes without calendar dates.

findings.title: Recurring ritual times at calendar adjustments
findings.paraphrase: In the first mystery mode, Steiner places ritual access to deities at selected calendar discrepancies, including end-of-year intervals and an eighteen-year lunar cycle. He ascribes to priests the preservation of powers received at these times for use during the rest of the year.

findings.title: From preserved ferments to the ritual Word
findings.paraphrase: Steiner distinguishes the solar radiance he attributes to the earlier vessels from the third mystery mode’s rhythmic ritual language and images in sacrificial smoke. He connects this third mode to Samothrace and describes later Masses as inheriting aspects of it.

findings.title: Christian Renewal and the fourth ritual mode
findings.paraphrase: Addressing the new priesthood, Steiner ties the fourth mystery mode to its inauguration at the first Goetheanum roughly two years before the lecture. He presents the rite and Apocalypse as linked subjects in the proposed religious renewal.

findings.title: Four churches as cultural continuations
findings.paraphrase: Steiner sees Ephesus as carrying elements of the first post-Atlantean period into Christianity, Smyrna as carrying the Persian inheritance, Pergamon as recalling the Hermetic third period and Thyatira as recalling the fourth period and Golgotha. These are typological associations.

findings.title: Sardis as a carried-forward seed and the pale horse of the fourth seal
findings.paraphrase: Steiner has the letter to Sardis carry an embryonic element for the fifth cultural period. He describes death entering human awareness under the fourth seal’s pale horse and reads the break in horse imagery as a sign of change in the fifth period.

findings.title: Consciousness soul and moral weight
findings.paraphrase: Steiner predicts that unrealized intentions and some forms of intellectual activity will increasingly be felt as draining. His account treats moral weight as inward experience of fate and suggests why clergy might need to attend to individual experience.

findings.title: Sardis, attention to individuality and cultivation of will
findings.paraphrase: Steiner uses Sardis’s white garments as an image for perceiving the individual behind outward social circumstances. He asks his priestly audience to cultivate will through the Apocalypse and contrasts that proposal with his own polemical account of Jesuit training.

findings.title: Olfaction, apperception and the Sardis example
findings.paraphrase: Steiner calls the human intellectual apparatus a transformed olfactory organ, singling out apperception, and attributes some plant fragrances to perceived planetary influences. This is his speculative example of stars at work within nature. The passage gives no evolutionary stage for the alleged organ transformation.

findings.title: Solar cycles in the account of plant and mineral colors
findings.paraphrase: Steiner distinguishes a daily, yearly and roughly 25,920-year solar cycle. He ascribes plant colors to the annual course and stone colors to the longest cycle, then calls on the audience to bring a sense of stellar agency and the solar Christ into the present. The color claims are esoteric.

findings.title: The locust and one-third imagery in Steiner’s fifth and sixth trumpets
findings.paraphrase: Steiner reads the locusts and the later killing in Revelation through a claim that some people lack a human I. He discusses several hypothetical origins in his esoteric scheme. This is dehumanizing historical material with no warrant for identifying, assessing or classifying anyone.

findings.title: Crusades and the oral transmission of cosmic Christianity
findings.paraphrase: Steiner describes earlier Christianity as centered on Gospel and liturgy and attributes a transmission of cosmic Christianity from East to West around the Crusades, mainly through oral tradition in his account. He places a seventh seal at this juncture.

findings.title: Numerical patterns at the threshold and collective figures
findings.paraphrase: Steiner treats seven as a method of observation and number as relevant at the threshold in his initiation model. He treats the sealed and saved figures as pertaining to his scheme of collective development and distinguishes them from individual destiny.

findings.title: The central form and loss of Atlantean clairvoyance
findings.paraphrase: Steiner makes the current physical form central in a 343-form series while putting the present period beyond that form’s internal midpoint. He connects the displacement to a loss of older clairvoyance around mid-Atlantis and places the Christ impulse within the resulting spiritually dark interval.

findings.title: Sorat and the two future beasts
findings.paraphrase: Steiner distinguishes those characterized by the seven-headed beast from the two-horned being he calls their seducer. He relates that agency to resistance to union with the Sun and to abuse of spiritual powers after the astral transition.
findings.chronological_placement: projected Earth development, exact subdivision unspecified

findings.title: Sorat’s name-number and four human members
findings.paraphrase: Steiner supplies a letter-number reading of 666 and relates the four signs to the physical, etheric and astral bodies and the lower I. The explanation describes symbolic retention and hardening of those members.

findings.title: Michael, the New Jerusalem and preparatory forms of Jupiter
findings.paraphrase: Steiner relates New Jerusalem to human activity that prepares future Jupiter forms. He assigns to Michael, as the Solar Genius’s representative, the overcoming and binding of the adversary. These are linked into a projected planetary transition through his Apocalypse reading.

dossiers.title: Etheric emergence and earliest responsiveness
dossiers.analysis: GA 11 VIII changes the reference point from preterrestrial astral life to etheric embodiment. Its hearing analogy describes a whole-body function.

dossiers.title: Differentiation of body and environment
dossiers.analysis: GA 11 VIII groups the first two epochs in one retrospective account. Its gradual cosmic separation in §10 should be read alongside the more detailed order in IX–X.

dossiers.title: Embodiment, differentiation and new inward powers
dossiers.analysis: GA 11 supplies descriptions of pre-division anatomy, local group development and a volcanic transition. GA 13 relates form, I, lunar withdrawal and agency without supplying a calendar.

dossiers.title: Memory, organization, independent thinking and transition
dossiers.analysis: Read the seven overlapping phases in GA 11 III alongside the broad account of altered life-body, oracle and sensory experience in GA 13 IV. The sources provide no exact alignment for every process.

dossiers.title: Post-Atlantean Earth epoch
dossiers.analysis: The seven cultural periods are nested within this Earth epoch. Dates describe Steiner’s typology and some are inferred using his period arithmetic. GA 13 allows cultural continuities across the boundaries.

dossiers.title: Sixth great Earth epoch
dossiers.analysis: GA 104 places the seven seals here after the War of All Against All. GA 104a treats early seals as astral images of transformed cultural fruits and sometimes moves back to the prewar cultures while discussing them.

dossiers.title: Seventh great Earth epoch
dossiers.analysis: The trumpet subdivisions complete the physical-form sequence in GA 104. The lecture then describes further forms on Earth before a later Earth condition of life. A full trumpet-by-trumpet case remains open.

dossiers.title: Ancient Indian cultural period
dossiers.analysis: Preserved Atlantean perception and its teaching provide a baseline for GA 13’s cultural account. The account explicitly distinguishes the first period from later India.

dossiers.title: Ancient Persian cultural period
dossiers.analysis: Earthly work and the visibility of spiritual activity in the sensory world replace earlier emphases in Steiner’s typology. Ancient Persian spiritual content is projected to recur in transformed form in the sixth period.

dossiers.title: Egypto-Chaldean cultural period
dossiers.analysis: Steiner groups several cultural settings in one typology while describing different initiation streams. The fifth culture is said to revisit earlier spiritual content with awakened individual faculties.

dossiers.title: Greco-Roman cultural period
dossiers.analysis: The mind or intellectual soul is the development foregrounded at the individual scale. GA 181 subdivides the period into three approximate intervals. GA 201 traces the cultural and Christological currents through the same time.

dossiers.title: Consciousness-soul cultural period
dossiers.analysis: The age grows out of earlier processes and is marked by an emphasis on consciously cultivated cognition and action. GA 185 assigns the consciousness soul and the sentient-soul analogy to different currents.

dossiers.title: Sixth post-Atlantean cultural period
dossiers.analysis: A projected consolidation of capacities prepared in the fifth. GA 106 connects the period with the transformed Persian current. GA 104 identifies Philadelphia with the growth of brotherly love.

dossiers.title: Seventh post-Atlantean cultural period
dossiers.analysis: A projected final culture within the fifth great Earth epoch. GA 106 compares it with the first period, while GA 13 emphasizes altered developmental opportunities and a subsequent upheaval.

dossiers.title: Old Saturn organ cross-reference
dossiers.analysis: The seven cosmic dossiers remain the primary stage studies. This supplement points to a targeted comparison of the Old Saturn and Atlantean heart accounts.
