comparisons.title: Timing and mechanism of reproductive differentiation
comparisons.comparison: GA 11 VI §§2–5 foregrounds densification and redirected soul force. GA 13 IV §§69–70 ties the beginning of structural differentiation to changed forces at Moon departure. An overlapping process is plausible. Exact equivalence of the causal sequences and their wording awaits German comparison. German confirms the separate emphases: GA 11 uses Verdichtung; GA 13 §70 calls the change Anfang der Trennung after lunar departure. The cross-work timing remains open.

comparisons.title: Two placements for Ahrimanic influence
comparisons.comparison: GA 13 IV §88 already connects Ahrimanic beings to fear in early Earth embodiment. IV §97 specifies a further mid-Atlantean distortion of sensory and postmortem experience. Treat the latter as a specific intensification, with the source naming both effects. The German preserves the distinction as well, and §97 expressly refers back to the beings already indicated.

comparisons.title: Brain and thinking organs have several developmental thresholds
comparisons.comparison: GA 11 VI §§8–9 distinguishes incomplete organ formation and readiness for spirit contact. GA 11 X §§3–6 links preparations to the fire mist and later use by Luciferic entities. GA 13 IV §99 links the Atlantean brain as an instrument of thought to physical–etheric union. The texts use different developmental predicates. Exact anatomical equivalence remains open. German distinguishes Anlage and readiness in GA 11 and later names the physische Gehirn in GA 13 §99.

comparisons.title: Early sight rudiments versus developed light perception
comparisons.comparison: GA 11 IX §7 puts first ocular rudiments after Sun separation. VII §3 characterizes light perception as comparatively late in the late pre-division account and later in individual development. Separate an organ rudiment, a function and its timing in a life before attempting an exact crosswalk. German GA 11 IX §7 speaks of Anlagen to the eyes, whereas VII §3 speaks of Lichtwahrnehmung.

comparisons.title: Named Atlantean phase and approximate midpoint
comparisons.comparison: GA 11 III §§16–19 assigns particular changes in misuse and judgment to successive named phases. GA 13 IV §§96–97 places a spreading crisis around mid-Atlantis without naming a subphase. The passages do not themselves identify the fourth GA 11 phase with the midpoint of GA 13.

comparisons.title: Formation of a soul member and its characteristic cultural development
comparisons.comparison: GA 13 IV §77 German names Bewusstseinsseele in early Earth differentiation. GA 185 VIII §§3–7 names fifth-age individual development of the consciousness soul and a concurrent humanity-wide analogy to the sentient soul. Keep early articulation, period emphasis and social typology at their stated scales.

comparisons.title: Calendar conventions and the Christological anchor
comparisons.comparison: GA 181 §2 alternates expressions referring to BCE, Golgotha and the founding of Christianity while giving approximate boundaries. GA 184 uses 747 and 1413 in a simple 2,160-year calculation and GA 201 distinguishes a second temporal scheme at Christ. Preserve the stated numbers as approximate and audit German calendar terminology and modern crossover arithmetic before treating the implied dates as exact. GA 346 VII §§3 and 14 preserves the two 333 formulations in German and both English views. See NX01.

comparisons.title: Philadelphia, the sixth seal and the sixth great Earth epoch
comparisons.comparison: GA 104 XI §17 assigns Philadelphia to a prewar subperiod. GA 104a II-9 §§10–11 then shifts from that cultural period to its supposed fruit in the sixth seal. Both lectures supply grounds to distinguish the scales. A complete concordance with GA 346 remains open.

comparisons.title: GA 13 and GA 104 stage and attribute formation of the soul members differently
comparisons.comparison: GA 13 IV §77 speaks of early differentiation of the astral body into three soul members before the Spirits of Form kindle the I. GA 104 IX §7 ascribes successive development of the soul members to dim work of the I on astral, etheric and physical bodies from Lemuria through late Atlantis. Germ and subsequent elaboration could account for part of the difference, but the sources do not establish that identification. Compare the German GA 104 and full argument in GA 13 next. GA 104 IX §7 German confirms the sequential attributions to astral, etheric and physical bodies. GA 104a II-12 §§3–5 repeats the association and explicitly discusses a preparatory stage.

comparisons.title: Two scales for the seven churches
comparisons.comparison: GA 104 III §§15–18 uses Ephesus as a representative of the first post-Atlantean culture. GA 346 VI §§11–14,27 also uses Ephesus for the first archangelic cycle near Golgotha. The latter lecture explicitly names intersecting scales, leaving the correspondences alongside one another.

comparisons.title: Ideal period arithmetic and 1924 qualifications on numerical regularity
comparisons.comparison: GA 184 uses 2,160-year arithmetic for the fourth culture. GA 346 VI §§8–10 says that regular numerical patterns loosen in the consciousness-soul age, while continuing to use related cycles. The latter does not specify a replacement end year for the fifth culture. Derived future labels remain approximate.

comparisons.title: Two heart rudiment accounts share a lion association
comparisons.comparison: GA 110 VIII §§6–8 names an Old Saturn heart rudiment in the Leo direction. GA 104 IX §§20–22 places the rudiment leading to the physical heart within an Atlantean lion group-soul account. An earlier warmth predisposition and a later etheric or physical elaboration are plausible successive thresholds. The passages do not directly identify one as the continuation of the other. Compare the German terminology and GA 110 IX before assigning a single inception. The German GA 104 IX §22 uses Anlage and explicitly says it became the later physical heart. This supports a distinction of thresholds within GA 104 while leaving the cross-cycle identification open.

comparisons.title: Several distinct claims about inception and expression of the I
comparisons.comparison: GA 13 IV §77 describes kindling by Spirits of Form in early terrestrial evolution. GA 104 VIII §§7–8 and IX §20 attach first-person expression or first I-soul impulse to the fifth Atlantean phase. GA 346 VII §3 attaches 333 CE to entry into the intellectual soul. Track the predicates separately. The exact relationship between the two purported firsts still requires direct comparison. The 333 CE expression and the years-after-Golgotha wording in GA 346 VII §14 also merit edition comparison. GA 346 XII §§23–24 adds its own distinction between mid-Atlantean solar activation and fourth-culture inward residence. See NX16.

comparisons.title: Later lunar and solar reunions across GA 13 and GA 104a
comparisons.comparison: GA 13 VI §§7–8 narrates lunar return and subsequent reunification of Earth with the Sun and other planets. GA 104a II-10 §5 describes a subtle Earth component reuniting with the Sun and the gross component combining with the Moon in the seventh-trumpet setting. The sources do not identify whether the accounts describe different phases or different versions. Keep their sequencing and qualified referents distinct.

comparisons.title: Two English versions retain a gap in the fifth-seal lecture
comparisons.comparison: GA 104a Oslo II-9 §6 ends with an omission marker in both the Steiner Online Library and Hindes English editions. II-10 §§1–2 recaps the fifth and sixth seals and moves to the seventh, while leaving the missing II-9 wording unverified. The German Oslo II-9 §6 also prints a gap marker at the same location. The origin and extent of the gap beyond this published record remain unknown.

comparisons.title: Calendar markers and other readings of 666
comparisons.comparison: GA 346 VII–VIII uses 666, 1332 and 1998 in a historical and prophetic sequence. GA 104a II-10 explains a name-number, and its broader sequence supplies another developmental context. The passages do not give one universal chronological rule. Oslo II-11 §§10–13 relates Sorat and 666 to projected separation and deliberately misused spiritual powers. GA 104 XI §§14–18 gives another calculation based on the sixth positions of multiple nested levels.

comparisons.title: Atlantis recurs at two different scales
comparisons.comparison: GA 346 XII §12 compares a Greco-Roman soul experience with earlier Atlantean physical experience. GA 104a II-10 §5 compares the whole seals epoch with a transformed Atlantis, stressing consciously regained clairvoyance. Both links can coexist with their separate scale and subject.

comparisons.title: Atlantean solar kindling and later residence of the I
comparisons.comparison: GA 346 XII §§23–24 describes growth of I-awareness from mid-Atlantis and later inward residence. GA 104 IX §20 names a first I-soul impulse in the fifth subgroup and GA 13 IV §77 describes earlier kindling in another account. Preserve the distinct predicates and avoid making the midpoint equal the fifth subdivision.

comparisons.title: GA 104 X §25 specifies the completed level in German
comparisons.comparison: The English opening of §25 can be read as three of 49 forms. German specifies die drei ersten Lebenszustände and the paragraph then enumerates seven forms in each. Within this scheme three completed life conditions yield 21 preceding Earth forms, before adding three forms of the fourth condition.

comparisons.title: Solar and lunar reunions in relation to future Earth rounds
comparisons.comparison: Oslo II-11 places solar reunion in the anticipated Jupiter condition within Earth. II-10 presents a split around the seventh trumpet. GA 13 VI gives lunar reunion before solar and the planetary transition. These sources use different sequences and referents. They do not furnish a secure one-to-one alignment.

comparisons.title: Babylon in the adjacent Oslo lectures and the 1924 course
comparisons.comparison: Oslo II-11 §15 places a fall or casting away in Venus-Earth. II-12 §14 speaks of Errettung and places the statement alongside another sixth-level image. GA 346 XI supplies a three-stage sequence with no direct Venus-Earth crosswalk in the checked passages. The German confirms that the differing predicates appear in the published text.

comparisons.title: Constitutional description and developmental agency answer different questions
comparisons.comparison: GA 121 III §§3–6 describes the three soul members as modifications within the astral body in a presentation of present organization. GA 104 IX §7 and GA 104a II-12 §4 discuss the processes of formation through different bodies. This makes a distinction of topic possible, while the particular sequence and agency difference between GA 13 IV §77 and GA 104 IX remains open.

comparisons.title: Watery differentiation and Sun separation occur in different narrated orders
comparisons.comparison: GA 11 IX §§5–7 describes watery substance and a combined water-air-ether condition before Sun separation. GA 13 IV §66 explicitly inserts separation from a fire-air Earth before incorporation of watery substance. A distinction between types of watery substance or narrative scales would require direct support. The checked English sequences differ.

comparisons.title: Sexual differentiation and its conscious perception are described at several thresholds
comparisons.comparison: GA 11 X §4 and GA 13 IV §70 place reproductive differentiation around lunar departure. GA 104 X §§38–40 describes an Atlantean threshold in conscious perception of sexuality and describes physical duality using its own head-and-horn imagery. The change in awareness is distinct. The full equivalence of the physical descriptions is unresolved.

comparisons.title: The historical trumpets and the later Earth trumpets belong to different scales
comparisons.comparison: GA 346 XIII §3 explicitly distinguishes a consciousness-soul strand from the general human development addressed in 1908. Its smaller historical sequence treats the Crusades as the shift to trumpets. GA 104 XI places the great trumpets epoch after the seals and after the War of All Against All. Keep both readings and retain the explicit distinction of scope.

comparisons.title: The 1940s wording is specific to the checked SOL English rendering
comparisons.comparison: GA 346 XIII German §§4–6 gives the early forties and 1843–44 before continuing with the same forties. German §23 says the sixth trumpet is being experienced at the time of the 1924 talk. Reading §6 as 1840s follows the nearest antecedent and fits §23. The alternate English view also continues with the forties after explicitly naming the 1840s. Record the SOL English wording and edition provenance.

comparisons.title: 1933, 1998 and multiple modern Apocalypse datings
comparisons.comparison: GA 346 XVI §§21–24 names 1933 in a comet and beast discussion. VIII §§20–24 puts a Sorat marker at 1998 and XIII relates a seventh trumpet to the late twentieth century on its narrower scale. The images and assigned predicates differ. The lectures do not specify a precise relation between the 1933 and 1998 markers.

comparisons.title: The internal scale of the ordinal 666 in GA 104 XI
comparisons.comparison: In §15 the sequence is described using life cycles and two subdivisions called great and small epochs. In §18 the last long phase is described by six completed life conditions and six forms within the seventh. The German confirms the change in terminology. The lecture clearly places 666 later than the trumpet transition, but the mapping of all three digits across these descriptions and to the date-bearing GA 346 sequence remains open. GA 104 XI §§21–31 now also has separate findings for the name-number, the two beasts and Michael. These passages connect the symbolic name to the distant separation without fixing the unresolved ordinal nesting.

comparisons.title: The fifth seal and Sardis on two time scales
comparisons.comparison: GA 346 V applies the fifth seal to the fifth cultural period alongside Sardis. GA 104 assigns the larger seven-seal sequence to the next great Earth epoch. GA 346 XIII expressly distinguishes its fourth- and fifth-period framework from the larger earlier reading.

comparisons.title: Saturn as deep trance and as inward wonder
comparisons.comparison: GA 104 X qualifies its deep-trance comparison as predominant and GA 11 XII distinguishes reach from clarity. GA 346 III describes warmth and inward wonder within early Saturn. The sources do not explicitly identify the subject or subdivision that would make wonder and trance descriptions of one phenomenological state.

comparisons.title: Collective numbers and individual destiny
comparisons.comparison: GA 346 XIII §§25–29 states that the numbers at the visionary threshold address collective evolution in Steiner’s scheme. GA 104 XI §§14–18 uses a numerical scheme to describe successive states and conditional separation. Numerical correspondence by itself supplies no identification or prediction about a specific person.

comparisons.title: Sorat name-number, ordinal sequence and dated recurrence
comparisons.comparison: GA 104 XI §§15–18 gives a future ordinal marker, §§21–25 gives the symbolic name-number and §31 connects Sorat with the final separation. GA 346 VIII §§20–24 uses a dated recurrence of the name-number. The shared symbol is directly attested. The descriptions leave the correspondence between the dated recurrence and the future ordinal scheme open.
